name: Lung-protective tidal volume reduction with rate compensation
explanation: Prompt reduction of tidal volume toward 6 mL/kg PBW (~400 mL) paired with rate increase prevents both volutrauma and severe acute respiratory acidosis.
source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8; ESICM ARDS Guidelines 2023

name: Delayed respiratory rate compensation after tidal volume reduction
explanation: Following tidal volume reduction toward 6 mL/kg PBW, the set respiratory rate was left low (<= 18 bpm) without compensation, allowing acute respiratory acidosis (pH < 7.25) to develop over subsequent minutes.
source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8; The Ventilator Book, 3rd ed.

name: Sound PEEP titration with unforeseen hemodynamic compromise
explanation: Increasing PEEP was clinically indicated by ARDSNet high-PEEP titration, but the patient experienced an unforeseen drop in preload and blood pressure (MAP < 65 mmHg) requiring fluid or vasopressor support.
source: ALVEOLI Study Group. N Engl J Med 2004;351:327-36; ATS Guidelines 2024

name: Empirical titration based on PBW and SpO2 before blood gas
explanation: Titrating ventilation based on predicted body weight and continuous pulse oximetry before laboratory arterial blood gas return is standard clinical practice under diagnostic delay.

name: PEEP optimization for recruitability
explanation: Increasing PEEP from 5 to 10-14 cmH2O recruits atelectatic lung units and improves PaO2/FiO2 in moderate-to-severe ARDS.
source: ALVEOLI Study Group. N Engl J Med 2004;351:327-36; ATS Guidelines 2024

name: Early prone positioning for severe ARDS
explanation: Prone positioning significantly improves ventilation-perfusion matching and reduces mortality when PaO2/FiO2 is persistently < 150.
source: Guérin C, et al. PROSEVA trial. N Engl J Med 2013;368:2159-68

name: Delayed prone positioning
explanation: Prone positioning was ordered late after sustained exposure to severe refractory hypoxaemia and high mechanical strain.
source: Guérin C, et al. PROSEVA trial. N Engl J Med 2013;368:2159-68

name: Failure to reduce injurious tidal volume in ARDS
explanation: Maintaining or increasing tidal volume >= 650 mL (almost 10 mL/kg PBW) causes excessive cyclical alveolar overdistension and barotrauma.
source: ARDS Network. N Engl J Med 2000;342:1301-8

name: Bronchodilator in acute parenchymal ARDS
explanation: Administering bronchodilators in the absence of bronchospasm or obstructive airway disease does not address diffuse alveolar damage or shunt.

name: Timely post-titration arterial blood gas
explanation: Reassessing blood gas within 15-30 minutes of major ventilator titration objectively verifies gas exchange response and safety limits.

name: Conservative PEEP titration under hemodynamic uncertainty
explanation: Selecting moderate PEEP (10-12 cmH2O) rather than aggressive high PEEP (>= 14 cmH2O) is clinically defensible when mean arterial pressure or right ventricular afterload is borderline, avoiding severe hemodynamic instability while providing lung recruitment.
source: ALVEOLI Study Group. N Engl J Med 2004;351:327-36; ESICM ARDS Guidelines 2023
